```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4.5)
```

```{r}
library(pgmcompR)
```

Exact inference computes posteriors such as $P(Q \mid E = e)$ without
approximation. pgmcompR offers three exact engines that must, and in the
test suite do, agree to machine precision: brute force enumeration (small
models only), variable elimination and the junction tree.

## Factors

Every discrete computation is expressed with factors: nonnegative tables
over a set of variables. Values are stored with the first variable varying
fastest.

```{r}
st <- list(A = c("a0", "a1"), B = c("b0", "b1", "b2"))
f <- discrete_factor(c("A", "B"), st, 1:6)
f
g <- discrete_factor("B", st["B"], c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2))
factor_product(f, g)
factor_marginalize(f, "B")
factor_reduce(f, list(B = "b1"))
factor_maximize(f, "A", argmax = TRUE)
```

State labels are part of a factor's identity. Two factors that disagree on
the states of a shared variable are never multiplied by position:

```{r, error = TRUE}
factor_product(g, discrete_factor("B", list(B = c("b2", "b1", "b0")), 1:3))
```

## Variable elimination

To answer a query, variable elimination multiplies the factors that mention
a variable, sums the variable out and repeats. The cost depends on the
elimination order, which `elimination_order()` chooses greedily.

```{r}
asia <- example_network("asia")
elimination_order(asia, "min_fill")
elimination_order(asia, "min_degree", variables = c("asia", "tub", "smoke"))
query(asia, "lung", list(xray = "yes", smoke = "yes"))
query(asia, "lung", list(xray = "yes", smoke = "yes"), method = "enumeration")
```

Before elimination, barren nodes (unobserved leaves outside the query) are
pruned, because their CPDs sum to one.

### Log space

Long chains of small probabilities underflow in double precision. With
`log = TRUE` the computation is carried out with log sum exp:

```{r}
evidence_probability(asia, list(xray = "yes", dysp = "yes"))
evidence_probability(asia, list(xray = "yes", dysp = "yes"), log = TRUE)
query(asia, "tub", list(xray = "yes"), log = TRUE)
```

### Soft evidence

Virtual (likelihood) evidence multiplies in a likelihood vector instead of
fixing a state: here the X-ray reader is only 70% sure that the film is
abnormal.

```{r}
query(asia, "lung", virtual_evidence = list(xray = c(no = 0.3, yes = 0.7)))
```

### Impossible evidence

Evidence of probability zero is an error with its own class, so callers can
catch it:

```{r, error = TRUE}
query(asia, "lung", list(tub = "yes", either = "no"))
evidence_probability(asia, list(tub = "yes", either = "no"))
```

## MAP and MPE

`mpe_query()` maximizes over all unobserved variables; `map_query()`
maximizes the marginal of a subset, summing the rest out first. They answer
different questions and can disagree.

```{r}
mpe_query(asia, list(dysp = "yes"))
map_query(asia, c("tub", "lung", "bronc"), list(dysp = "yes"))
```

## Junction trees

When many queries share the same evidence, the junction tree pays the cost
once. Moralize, triangulate, connect the maximal cliques by a maximum weight
spanning tree, then calibrate by message passing.

```{r}
jt <- junction_tree(asia)
jt
cal <- calibrate(jt, list(xray = "yes"))
clique_beliefs(cal)[[1]]
query(asia, c("tub", "lung"), list(xray = "yes"), method = "jt")
```

After calibration, neighboring cliques agree on their separator marginals,
and any single variable marginal can be read from a clique that contains it.

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE)}
plot(jt)
```

## Graph utilities used by inference

```{r}
m <- moralize(asia)
is_chordal(m)
tri <- triangulate(m, heuristic = "min_fill")
tri$cliques
d_separated(asia, "tub", "smoke", "lung")
active_trail_nodes(asia, "smoke", z = "dysp")
```
